drawdown_context: Mortgage REIT, multifamily bridge lender. FY24 10-K (filed 2025-03-03) reports first full-year GAAP net loss in years (-$412M continuing ops vs +$351M 2023), EPS -$2.52, book value per common share unchanged at $10.61 (after a $14.10 -> $10.61 collapse in 2023), and 2024 dividend cut from $0.30/qtr to $0.25 in 2H24. Subsequent Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-05-09, 6 days pre-cutoff) further cut dividend to $0.125/qtr (-50%) and discloses non-accrual UPB exploded from $654.5M to $1,129.9M (+73%) in a single quarter. Forward return -57.5% confirms the cycle was not bottoming.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Audit Report (Deloitte & Touche, 3/3/2025): unqualified opinion. Critical Audit Matter is 'Allowance for loan losses - Refer to Notes 3 and 6.' No going-concern paragraph, no substantial-doubt language anywhere in the 10-K (grep on substantial doubt / going concern / cease operations: 0 hits in disclosure language).
rfm_tuples.f: going_concern_local on 10-K AND on the most-recent-pre-cutoff 10-Q (filed 2025-05-09); Mode B: did the next periodic filing escalate disclosure?
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K: signal=NO_GOING_CONCERN, n_matches=0. Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-05-09): also NO_GOING_CONCERN despite credit deterioration; CAM (allowance) is the only flagged area. Auditor Deloitte since 2012 (13yr tenure, no resignation/disagreement language).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Unlike WOLF, management did NOT escalate to going-concern between 10-K and Q1 10-Q. The disclosure is technically clean and the auditor stayed. But the auditor's sole Critical Audit Matter is the allowance for loan losses — i.e. the very thing that subsequently exploded in Q1 (allowance moved $339.9M -> $239.2M only because of large charge-offs, while non-accruals grew 73% QoQ). The CAM was a pre-warning that the auditor itself flagged the reserves as judgmentally fragile.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Note 6: Allowance for loan losses ending balance $339.9M (Dec'24) vs $101.6M (Dec'23). FY24 provision for loan losses = $252.2M (vs $8.7M in 2023, a 29x jump). Bridge segment allowance: $36.2M -> $170.4M (+371%). Construction allowance: $30.9M -> $140.1M (+354%, of which $137.8M is 'Specific'). FY24 charge-offs $14.6M.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on 10-K + Q1 10-Q roll-forward; Mode B: did reserve build front-run real losses, or under-reserve? Compare specific reserves to non-accrual UPB and to subsequent charge-offs.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K: allowance vs non-accrual UPB = $339.9M / $654.5M = 51.9% coverage. Specific reserves alone ($187.6M) cover only 28.7% of non-accrual UPB. Q1 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-05-09): allowance dropped to $239.2M (charge-offs realized losses) but non-accrual UPB grew to $1,129.9M -> coverage collapsed to 21.2%. Bridge allowance $170.4M -> $31.0M; Construction allowance $140.1M -> $166.1M (specific $146.3M).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K's massive reserve build looked like aggressive front-running of losses; the Q1 10-Q reveals it was inadequate. Non-accrual UPB grew 73% QoQ while allowance fell 30% QoQ as charge-offs flushed through. The 'reserves are conservative' implicit framing of the 10-K was reversed within 9 weeks — coverage ratio went from 52% to 21%. Mode B: the FY24 provision was reactive (cleaning up prior under-reserving) rather than forward-looking — losses kept coming.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Item 5: 'Declaration Date... Dividend per Share. December 14, 2023 ... $0.30. March 15, 2024 ... $0.30. June 14, 2024 ... $0.30. September 13, 2024 ... $0.25. December 13, 2024 ... $0.25.' Cover discussion: 'Distributable earnings $28,360 [thousand]... Distributable earnings per common share - diluted $0.07. Dividends declared per common share $1.10. Dividend yield 14.7%.'
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on dividend coverage; Mode B: is the FY24 dividend covered by distributable earnings? If not, is the cut already announced sufficient?
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24 dividend declared $1.10/share against distributable EPS of $0.07/share — coverage ratio 6.4%. Even ex-realized-losses ('distributable earnings before realized losses' $0.97/share) coverage is only 88%. Q1 2025 10-Q: distributable EPS -$0.09 (negative), dividend cut to $0.125/qtr (-50% from $0.25, -58% from $0.30 the year before). Q1 dividend payable on balance sheet fell from $43.2M to $23.9M.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: FY24 dividend was paid out of capital, not earnings — distributable earnings covered only 6% of declared dividend. Q1 2025 cut to $0.125 still produced negative distributable EPS, meaning even the cut dividend was not covered. Market-implied dividend yield of 14.7% at year-end was the market correctly pricing the dividend as unsustainable. The 10-K's narrative of 'we use distributable earnings to determine dividends' is contradicted by the actual payout ratio.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K MD&A operating-results table: 'Book value per common share $10.61 $10.61 $14.10' for FY24, FY23, FY22. Net loss from continuing operations $412.0M (FY24) vs net income $351.2M (FY23). Return on equity from continuing ops -19.6% (FY24) vs +17.2% (FY23). Q1 2025 10-Q: 'Book value per common share $10.61 $13.44'.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on book-value evolution + claim_evolution between 10-K and 10-Q; Mode B: does flat BVPS in 2024 reconcile with -$412M GAAP loss, or is there equity issuance / OCI offset hiding erosion?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Common shares outstanding grew from 162.8M (Dec'23) to 172.5M (Dec'24) — 6.0% dilution. Stated BVPS unchanged at $10.61 (FY24 = FY23) despite $412M loss; reconciliation implies ~$300M+ of share issuance, OCI / paid-in-capital movements covered the GAAP loss. Q1 2025 10-Q reveals BVPS prior-year-end comparable was $13.44 (vs $14.10 disclosed in 10-K for Dec'22) — the 'flat' BVPS in the 10-K table was achieved via Broadmark merger accounting / preferred preference adjustments; underlying common-equity erosion is closer to 25% from peak. Implied price/book at 5/15/2025 prices: stock around $4-5 against $10.61 stated BVPS = market-implied haircut of 50%+.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: BVPS was held 'flat' on the surface via share issuance and merger accounting masking — but $412M of GAAP losses don't vanish without equity erosion. The market priced the stock at <50% of stated book, which is the implied-verification signal: market does not believe the carried allowance/fair-value marks. Combined with the bargain-purchase gain ($102.5M) recognized in Q1 2025 — a non-cash earnings item — the FY24 BVPS line is a managed number.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Note 6: 'During the year ended December 31, 2024, the Company entered into 65 loan modifications with an aggregate carrying value of $1.0 billion, or 12.4% of total loans, net... 30 loans with an aggregate carrying value of $688.8 million, or 8.2% of loans, net, that were modified to include both term extensions and interest payment deferrals.' 'Loans with modifications disclosed in the previous twelve months are performing in accordance with their modified terms... except for 12 loans with a carrying value of $43.7 million.'
rfm_tuples.f: self_text + claim_evolution: are modifications curing real distress (Mode A: existence) or hiding non-accruals (Mode B: implied check — what is the re-default rate?)
rfm_tuples.M_value: 12.4% of total loans were modified in FY24 alone — extension activity for a bridge lender of this scale typically signals borrower inability to refinance into permanent. 12 of those mods ($43.7M) re-defaulted within 3 months — re-default rate 4.4% on a 12-month look-back base. Bridge book modified percentage even higher given construction also re-extends. Q1 2025 10-Q: an additional 23 modifications in Q1 alone, on top of FY24's 65 — annualized run-rate of 92 modifications vs 65 in FY24. Non-accruals also grew from $526.8M (FY24) to $848.4M (Q1'25) — so modifications were not stabilizing the book; they were extending the runway while underlying credit deteriorated.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: 'Substantially all modified loans performing' is the textbook bank-fraud signal — a 12-bps re-default rate disclosed early in the cycle is rarely the equilibrium rate. By Q1 2025, modification pace was accelerating AND non-accruals were exploding — i.e. modifications were not preventing the next wave of defaults, they were simply moving non-accrual recognition forward by one or two quarters. This is the canonical 'extend and pretend' pattern.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Note 11: 'The table below presents the contractual maturities for senior secured notes and corporate debt: 2025 $120,000; 2026 $760,884; 2027 $100,000; 2028 $110,000; 2029 $225,000.' Includes $350M of 4.50% Senior Secured Notes due 2026 and 9.00% Senior Notes due 2029 (issued Dec 2024).
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on debt maturity wall; Mode B: did the company issue 9% retail baby bonds in 2024 (distress pricing) and is the 2026 wall covered by liquidity?
rfm_tuples.M_value: $760.9M of corporate debt matures in 2026. December 10, 2024 8-K confirms RC issued $130M of 9.00% senior notes due 2029 at $25-par retail bond structure (Morgan Stanley/Piper Sandler/RBC/UBS/Wells Fargo). 9% senior unsecured coupon for a 5-year tenor was deeply off-market in late 2024 (treasuries ~4.2%, comparable IG mREIT issuance was 6-7%). Cash on balance sheet $143.8M at Dec'24 against $760M 2026 maturity. Q1 2025: cash improved to $182.8M but still far below maturity wall.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: 9.00% retail-bond pricing in Dec 2024 is the bond-market's verdict on credit. The $760M 2026 wall is ~5x year-end cash and requires either securitization issuance, asset sales, or refinancing at distress coupons. The 10-K's disclosure of the maturity ladder was technically complete but did not frame the 9% coupon as a distress signal — readers had to cross-reference the 8-K to see it. Mode B: blue-chip mREITs (BXMT, STWD) were funding at 6-7% in same period; the 200-300bps spread to peers is the implied verification.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Note 6 delinquency table: Bridge segment, 60+ days past due $521.8M (Dec'23) -> $276.2M (Dec'24). Non-accrual loans $526.8M (Dec'24) vs $633.9M (Dec'23). Total loans 60+ days past due $389.3M of $8.3B (4.7%) vs $915.6M of $10.6B (8.6%) in 2023.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text + claim_evolution: do the IMPROVED delinquency numbers in 10-K reflect real cure or just charge-off / NPL transfer?
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K's improving delinquency narrative is reversed in Q1 2025 10-Q: non-accrual UPB jumped from $654.5M (Dec'24) to $1,129,944K (Mar'25) — +72.6% in 90 days. Non-accruals 'with an allowance': $509.8M -> $797.7M (+56%). 'Without an allowance' (most severe): $17.0M -> $50.7M (+198%). Q1 charge-offs and the loan-portfolio shrinkage (total loans $8.3B at Dec'24 -> portfolio further shrinking in Q1 as $729M was transferred to held-for-sale per 10-K cash-flow statement) show management was actively shrinking the book under duress.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K's 'improved' year-over-year delinquency comparison was artifact of having charged off / transferred-to-HFS the prior cohort, NOT cure. Q1 2025's 73% QoQ non-accrual jump is the implied-verification dispositive fact: the multifamily-bridge distress cycle was ACCELERATING into 2025, not stabilizing. The framework's claim_evolution check catches the divergence between 10-K's narrative (which framed FY24 as the trough) and Q1's data (which showed it was an interior point, not a peak).

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Item 9B: 'None of our officers and directors entered into, modified or terminated any "Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangements"... during the quarter ended December 31, 2024.' Implicit claim: insider behavior is routine.
rfm_tuples.f: form4 / insider_vs_calendar around capital events (Dec 10 2024 $130M 9% notes issuance, Jan 16 2025 $150M buyback authorization, March 3 2025 10-K, May 8 2025 Q1 release); Mode B: did insiders BUY to signal confidence, or sell?
rfm_tuples.M_value: 43 Form 4s pre-cutoff (Jan'24 - May'25). Tx codes: 21 A (awards), 18 F (forfeit/withhold), 12 P (open-market purchase), 9 M (exercise). ZERO open-market sales. 12 open-market PURCHASES, all clustered around / just after the 10-K filing March 3-12, 2025. CEO Capasse $497K (100,000 sh @ $4.8-5.0); President Ross $24K; CFO Ahlborn $50K; CCO Zausmer $54K; COO Taylor $52K; director Nathan $26K + earlier 2024 buys $253K; director Luebbers $42K. Total open-market insider purchases: ~$999K.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Form 4 pattern is genuinely on the BULLISH side for distress — no insider sales, multiple insiders making token open-market buys around the bad earnings report. However, the dollar amounts are ritualistic (CEO $497K = under 1% of his net worth at his comp level; CFO/COO/CCO all bought identical 10,000-share / ~$50K parcels — coordinated 'signal' buys, not conviction). The total $1M of buying is dwarfed by the $130M of 9% notes the company simultaneously raised — i.e. management would not put real money in but would issue 9% paper. Mode B: insider purchase signal is structurally weak when the buyers are simultaneously approving distressed capital actions.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K Note 6 collateral concentration table: 'Multi-family 60.1%, SBA 14.6%, Mixed Use 9.5%, Industrial 4.8%, Retail 4.1%, Office 3.2%, Lodging 2.0%.' Geographic: Texas 19.3%, California 10.8%, Florida 7.9%, Arizona 7.7%, Oregon 7.3%, Georgia 6.7%. LTV: 'average loan-to-value (LTV) on the originated portfolio was 68.3%. The weighted average LTV of our acquired loans was 80.4%.'
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on concentration; Mode B: 60% multifamily concentration + 19% Texas + average 80% LTV on acquired book is the textbook 'bridge to nowhere' setup of the 2021-2022 vintage. Cross-check vintage table.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Bridge book by vintage: 2021 vintage $2,270.5M, 2022 vintage $2,083.7M (combined $4.35B = 85% of $5.1B bridge book). 2021-2022 were peak-cap-rate-compression vintages where multifamily bridge loans were underwritten at 3.5-4% cap rates that have since blown out 200+ bps. 60+ days past due by vintage at Dec'24: $101.2M (2021) and $178.7M (2022) — 60% of all bridge delinquency in those two vintages, but only 12% of carrying value yet impaired, suggesting more to come as 2-3yr bridge terms hit maturity. Sun Belt concentration (TX 19.3% + AZ 7.7% + FL 7.9% + GA 6.7% = 41.6%) is exactly where multifamily rent declines were sharpest in 2024.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The disclosure is technically complete, but the FRAMING ('diversified across 50 states') buries the lede: 60% multifamily, 86% of bridge book in 2021-2022 vintages, 42% Sun Belt — this is a concentrated bet on the exact cohort that was distressed at the cutoff date. The 80.4% average LTV on the ACQUIRED book (from Broadmark merger) is functionally underwater after 2024 cap-rate moves. The 10-K does not directly state this. Mode B: cross-referencing the vintage table with the geographic and collateral concentration tables reveals a much more concentrated risk than the high-level narrative suggests.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K MD&A / Item 8 cash-flow statement: 'Loans transferred from loans, net to loans, held for sale $729,016' (FY24, in thousands) vs $3,641 (FY23). 'Valuation allowance, loans held for sale $97,620 and $0' on balance sheet. Implies $729M of loans were moved off the held-for-investment book and marked down via $97.6M valuation allowance.
rfm_tuples.f: self_text on HFI -> HFS transfers; Mode B: $729M transfer with $97.6M valuation allowance = ~13% mark-down — what does this imply about the remaining held-for-investment book carried at amortized cost?
rfm_tuples.M_value: Mass transfer of $729M from amortized-cost book to HFS at 13% haircut. Q1 2025 10-Q: 'Bargain purchase gain $102.5M' suggests the UDF IV transaction (announced Nov 29 2024, closed Q1 2025) booked a $102M GAIN — i.e. the assets acquired from UDF IV were carried at $102M below management's estimated fair value, used to offset operating losses. UDF IV merger structured with CVRs at 60% of tangible book — i.e. the acquired assets were marked at a discount that triggered a non-cash earnings credit.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Two parallel signals: (1) Management was selectively transferring loans to HFS and marking them down 13% — implying the held-for-investment book carried at amortized cost is overstated by some unknown but similar magnitude; the auditor's CAM on allowance is the audit-side acknowledgement. (2) The Q1 2025 'bargain purchase gain' is a quality-of-earnings flag: $102M of non-cash income from UDF IV merger accounting smoothed an otherwise-negative quarter. Mode B: both reveal that 'fair value' is being applied selectively — aggressively (high allowance) on assets being divested, conservatively (amortized cost, lower allowance) on assets retained.

going_concern_10q_post_10k.note: Q1 10-Q did NOT escalate to going-concern, unlike WOLF. Distress is real but management still presenting as solvent.

summary: Ready Capital's FY24 10-K is a TECHNICALLY HONEST distress disclosure that nonetheless materially understates the trajectory. The auditor (Deloitte, 13yr tenure) gave a clean opinion with the Critical Audit Matter pointed exactly at allowance for loan losses — which subsequently halved in coverage as non-accrual UPB jumped 73% QoQ in Q1 2025. Mode A verification: most claims are quantitatively supported in the filings (no fraud signal, no auditor change, no going-concern language). Mode B (the strongest signals here): (1) dividend paid at 6% coverage out of capital; (2) 9.00% retail baby bond issued Dec 2024 = bond market's verdict on credit; (3) 12.4% of loans modified in FY24 with re-default already emerging — extend-and-pretend; (4) $729M loans transferred to HFS at 13% mark, implying held-for-investment book is over-marked; (5) Q1 10-Q reveals FY24 was not the trough — non-accruals exploded 73% in 90 days; (6) bargain-purchase gain $102M from UDF IV merger smoothed Q1 losses with non-cash income; (7) 86% of bridge book is 2021-2022 Sun Belt multifamily — the exact cohort in distress. The framework should correctly flag this as DISTRESSED despite the clean audit — the implied-verification signals (dividend coverage, bond pricing, claim evolution to Q1 10-Q, modification re-default rate) are the dispositive evidence that the 10-K's framing of FY24 as a cycle trough was wrong by the time the ink dried. Honesty-alpha framing: management is not lying, but they are obscuring the slope of deterioration. Strong short/avoid signal that the framework can capture pre-cutoff.
